project.name: Cluckwork
project.summary: Software for running an egg farm: record each day's eggs, feed and water per flock, track egg lots from the hen to the sale, sell to customers, log expenses and see the farm's numbers. One server (C# / .NET) serves both the web app (React) and its data, and stores everything in Postgres.

flows.title: Recording a day's eggs
flows.description: A staff member counts and grades a house's eggs, which creates egg lots and updates the dashboard.

steps.note: On the Daily entry screen, a worker enters collection and grading counts for a flock and taps Submit day.
The app sends the day's counts to the server.
The daily-entry request handler checks who is asking and hands the counts to the business rules.
Egg operations checks the counts balance, then turns the graded eggs into egg lots, blocked if the flock is under a medication hold.
The new entry and lots are saved.
Everything is written in one transaction, scoped to this farm.
The records land in the database; the dashboard's totals now include them.
Staff pick a customer and products and record the sale.
The sale is sent to the server.
The sales request handler passes it on.
Prices and discount limits are checked, and egg stock is drawn down from saleable lots.
The sale and the stock movement are saved.
Stored for reports and traceability back to the hen.
A connected AI assistant, signed in with a token the user approved, calls a farm tool.
The tool checks the token's permissions and turns the call into the same action the web app would take.
The same business rules run, so the AI app can't do anything a person couldn't.
The result is saved like any other record.

tour.title: What Cluckwork is
tour.note: An egg-farm management app. Staff use this web app on a computer or phone to record each day, manage stock and sell eggs.

tour.title: One main server
tour.note: A single server answers every request from the app, serves the app itself, and offers farm tools to connected AI assistants.

tour.title: The business rules
tour.note: Each farm area (eggs, flocks, sales, supplies, expenses) has its own rules for what's allowed and what happens. This is the heart of the app.

tour.title: Storage and background work
tour.note: Saves everything in Postgres, keeps each farm's data apart, and runs background jobs.

tour.title: The database
tour.note: All farm records, users and the activity log live here. Redis holds short-lived shared counters.

tour.title: The most-used screen
tour.note: Daily entry: where a day's eggs are counted and graded. Submitting it creates the egg lots everything else depends on.
